title: review
description: Stage output contract: the PR was reviewed against the task goal and code quality.

tests_meaningful.description: independent test-validate verdict (#13): do the change's tests meaningfully exercise it (would they fail if it regressed)? An explicit false rejects the review even when approved — the reviewer is a different agent from the one that wrote the tests, which is the point. Answer it whenever there are tests to read; omit it (or answer null) ONLY when the change has genuinely no test surface. An absent/null answer fails OPEN but is recorded as 'not judged' — never as a pass — and is evented (test_validation_skipped) when the TEST stage did not judge it either (#261)

severity.description: suggestion-only rejections auto-approve (the severity gate); critical/important drive the fix cycle

issues.description: blocking issues (empty when approved). Prefer the structured object form — severity gates disposition, file/line/suggested_fix make the fix cycle actionable

non_blocking.description: findings that do NOT block approval; each carries a `disposition` that gates what the engine does with it at finalize. Only `file` (or an absent disposition, for backward compatibility) becomes a deferred-scope issue — and only up to a small per-task cap; `fix_now`/`drop` findings are surfaced in the completion note ('Noted, not filed') but never filed, so nothing is silently dropped (empty if none)

disposition.description: filing threshold. `file`: a maintainer would put this on the backlog independently — out-of-scope (different subsystem / needs its own design) OR non-trivial (real work/risk). NEVER `file` these — they are `drop` (or `fix_now` if trivial-in-blast-radius): cosmetic consistency ('move X to match Y', rename for symmetry), speculative tunability (expose N knobs nobody asked for), premature instrumentation (dashboards/metrics for a feature not yet exercised), redundant convenience (a wrapper for already-exposed capability). `fix_now`: a trivial nit WITHIN the blast radius of this change (a docstring the edit made stale, a guard/type on a touched line) the implementer should have absorbed in place — not worth a ticket. `drop`: a real-but-untracked observation, noted and moved on. Absent disposition defaults to `file` (backward-compatible).

improvement.description: self-improvement loop: the single highest-value forward-looking improvement this task suggests for the PROJECT/roadmap (not a fix for this PR). Emit one ONLY if a maintainer would independently prioritize it — a concrete trigger or demonstrated need, not a nice-to-have. Do NOT emit: speculative tunability (expose N knobs nobody asked for), premature instrumentation (dashboards for a feature not yet exercised), or convenience wrappers for already-exposed capability. Omit if none clears the bar (it is optional). The engine files a `file`/absent-disposition improvement as an enhancement issue at finalize.

disposition.description: same filing threshold as a non_blocking finding, plus `fixup`. `file` (or absent, backward-compatible): file as an enhancement issue. `fixup`: apply as a trivial in-place change in THIS PR — do not file. `fix_now`/`drop`: surfaced in the completion note, not filed. Absent defaults to `file`.

retrospective.description: self-improvement loop: one lesson this task teaches about the ORCHESTRATION PROCESS (prompts/stages/tooling/lanes), not the code. Rendered in the completion note. Omit if none.

detail.description: what we learned / what to change
